title: PRELIMINARY RECKONING
opening: The words of Sun the Master:
firstContentParagraph: To all nations War is a great matter. Upon the army death or life depend: it is the means of the existence or destruction of the State.
ending: If the condition of both sides with regard to these matters be known, I can foretell the victor.

title: OPERATIONS OF WAR
firstContentParagraph: Now the requirements of war are such that we need a thousand light chariots with four horses each; a thousand leather-covered chariots, and one hundred thousand armoured men; and we must send supplies to distant fields. Wherefore the cost at home and in the field, the entertainment of guests, glue and lacquer for repairs, and necessities for the upkeep of waggons and armour are such that in one day a thousand pieces of gold are spent. With that amount a force of one hundred thousand men can be raised:--you have the instruments of victory.
ending: The good general is the lord of the people's lives, the guardian of the country's welfare.

title: THE ATTACK BY STRATAGEM
firstContentParagraph: Now by the laws of war, better than defeating a country by fire and the sword, is to take it without strife.
ending: It has been said aforetime that he who knows both sides has nothing to fear in a hundred fights; he who is ignorant of the enemy, and fixes his eyes only on his own side, conquers, and the next time is defeated; he who not only is ignorant of the enemy, but also of his own resources, is invariably defeated.

title: THE ORDER OF BATTLE
firstContentParagraph: The ancient masters of war first made their armies invincible, then waited until the adversary could with certainty be defeated.
ending: Such are the orders of battle.

title: THE SPIRIT OF THE TROOPS
firstContentParagraph: The control of large numbers is possible, and like unto that of small numbers, if we subdivide them.
ending: If the general be skilful, the spirit of his troops is as the impetus of a round stone rolled from the top of a high mountain.

title: EMPTINESS AND STRENGTH
firstContentParagraph: To be the first in the field, and there to await the enemy, is to husband strength.
ending: Among the five elements there is no settled precedence; the four seasons come and go; the days are long and short; and the moon waxes and wanes. So in war there is no fixity.

title: THE NINE CHANGES
firstContentParagraph: In general, the procedure of war is:--the Leader, having received orders from his lord, assembles the armies.
ending: These five faults in the leader are disastrous in war. The overthrow of the army and the slaughter of the general arise from them. Therefore they must be carefully considered.

title: THE EMPLOYMENT OF SPIES
firstContentParagraph: Calling 100,000 men to arms, and transporting them a hundred leagues, is such an undertaking that in one day 1,000 taels of the citizens' and nobles' money are spent; commotions arise within and without the state; carriers fall down exhausted on the line of march of the army; and the occupations of 700,000 homes are upset.
ending: Wherefore, intelligent rulers and wise generals use the cleverest men as spies, and invariably acquire great merit. The spy is a necessity to the army. Upon him the movement of the army depends.
